# markerdata: Marker Data Sets for Breeding Simulation

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/fernandes-lab/markerdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fernandes-lab/markerdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

markerdata provides curated single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) marker
panels drawn from public genomic resources across crops, trees, livestock,
fish and two sample-only reference species (the table below lists every
data set and species). Each panel is a
plain data frame with five marker-metadata columns (`snp`, `allele`, `chr`,
`pos`, `cm`) followed by one `-1`/`0`/`1` genotype column per individual, so
it can be used directly as founder genotypes for breeding-program simulation
with `simplePHENOTYPES::as_population()` or with breedingDesigner.

Every data set works offline. One small maize panel is bundled whole; each
of the other data sets ships a sample (2,000 SNPs, every individual; 1,000 SNPs for the four largest)
that loads instantly. For all but two of them, `marker_data(name, full = TRUE)`
downloads the whole panel on first use and caches it locally, and
`marker_download()` fetches every hosted whole panel at once (about 19 MB).
`Arabidopsis_div` (1001 Genomes) and `Human_div` (1000 Genomes Project) are
**sample only**: markerdata does not host their whole data sets, and
`marker_catalog()$source_url` gives the original download.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("markerdata")  # once on CRAN
remotes::install_github("fernandes-lab/markerdata")
```

## Usage

List every data set in the catalog and see which ones are already available
on this machine:

```{r}
library(markerdata)
marker_catalog()[, c("name", "common_name", "n_snp", "n_ind", "het", "mating", "available")]
```

The bundled maize panel loads without any download:

```{r}
head(marker_data("SNP55K_maize282_maf04")[, 1:8])
```

Every other panel returns its bundled sample by default, also without any
download:

```{r}
dim(marker_data("Cattle_div"))
```

Ask for the whole panel with `full = TRUE`; it is downloaded on first use
and cached afterward. To download every whole panel in one go, call
`marker_download()`. The `-1`/`0`/`1` genotype coding is exactly what
`simplePHENOTYPES::as_population()` expects for founder genotypes:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
geno <- marker_data("Cattle_div", full = TRUE)
pop <- simplePHENOTYPES::as_population(geno, individuals = 1:100)

marker_download() # every hosted whole panel
```

## Data sets

```{r, echo = FALSE}
cat <- marker_catalog()

fmt_download <- function(bytes, bundled, url) {
  ifelse(bundled, "bundled",
    ifelse(is.na(bytes), sprintf("sample only; [original data](%s)", url),
      sprintf("%.1f MB", bytes / 1e6)))
}

link_dois <- function(reference, doi) {
  refs <- strsplit(reference, ";\\s*")[[1]]
  dois <- strsplit(doi, ";\\s*")[[1]]
  n <- max(length(refs), length(dois))
  refs <- rep_len(refs, n)
  parts <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    if (i <= length(dois) && !is.na(dois[i]) && nzchar(dois[i])) {
      sprintf("%s [%s](https://doi.org/%s)", refs[i], dois[i], dois[i])
    } else {
      refs[i]
    }
  }, character(1))
  paste(parts, collapse = "; ")
}

tbl <- data.frame(
  `Data set` = cat$name,
  Species = cat$species,
  Panel = cat$panel,
  `SNPs x individuals` = paste0(
    format(cat$n_snp, big.mark = ","), " x ", format(cat$n_ind, big.mark = ",")
  ),
  `Heterozygous calls` = sprintf("%.1f%%", cat$het * 100),
  Mating = cat$mating,
  License = cat$license,
  `Full download` = fmt_download(cat$bytes, cat$bundled, cat$source_url),
  Reference = mapply(link_dois, cat$reference, cat$doi),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(tbl, row.names = FALSE)
```

Sizes are those of the whole panels, except for `Arabidopsis_div` and
`Human_div`, where the counts describe the sample because the whole data
set is not hosted (follow the link in the last-but-one column). The human data
are from publicly released, consented 1000 Genomes samples and are included
for method development and teaching. The bundled sample of each panel
is 2,000 SNPs (1,000 for `SoySNP50K_div`, `Cattle_div`, `Wheat_div` and `SugarBeet_div`, to keep the package small) and every individual of the panel: SNPs
evenly spaced over those polymorphic among the individuals.

Two data sets need care. `Potato_div` is an autotetraploid stored
**diploidized** (dosage 0 becomes `-1`, dosage 4 becomes `1`, dosages 1 to 3
become `0`), so its allele dosage is lost; `Sugarcane_div` holds the
diploid-style calls of its source (no dosage exists) at *Sorghum bicolor*
positions. Their help topics explain what is lost. Whole panels are hosted in
the GitHub releases `data-v1` and `data-v2` (the `release` column of
`marker_catalog()` says which).

## Cache

Downloaded whole panels are cached under `marker_cache_dir()`, which resolves
(in order) `getOption("markerdata.cache")`, the environment variable
`MARKERDATA_CACHE`, or else `tools::R_user_dir("markerdata", "cache")`. Use
`marker_download()` to fetch one or more data sets ahead of time (for
example before working offline), and `marker_cache_clear()` to remove cached
files again.

## Citing

Cite the package itself with `citation("markerdata")`. Every data set keeps
its own original license and must be cited on its own terms; get its
citation with `marker_references("<name>")`, e.g.
`marker_references("Rice_div")`.
